content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm facing a new issue while assembling the control panel for the filtration unit. It's almost complete, but I've discovered that the valves on the pneumatic terminal use an npn wiring scheme. Is there a way to connect them directly, without using additional relays, since there’s no extra space in the cabinet for more relays? A follow-up: The wiring diagrams for the [product_name] relay show that the positive wire connects to the contacts and is switched. Is it possible to connect part of the relay to the positive and part to the negative terminal? Are these contacts internally connected within [product_name]?

The relay contacts in [product_name] are floating, or potential-free. This means neither side of a relay contact is fixed to any potential, and the contacts themselves aren't permanently linked. Each relay contact can be assigned any voltage or potential up to 230 VAC to switch as needed.
Thank you, that's very helpful. For NPN sensors—am I right in thinking they actually can't be used in this setup?
It's actually possible to use NPN sensors in this configuration.
Wishing you the best! I appreciate your help so much. Thank you!
Please note: If you use NPN inputs as shown in the example for ixo65, the input signal will be inverted. If the sensor output is 1 (on), [product_name] will register it as a 0 (off).

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are clarifying how to wire relay outputs and inputs of [product_name] with NPN-type devices, especially in situations with limited cabinet space. The discussion centers on using the floating (potential-free) contacts of the relay for flexible wiring arrangements and managing signal inversion when connecting NPN devices, ideally without relying on extra relays.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to connect NPN sensors and actuators directly to [product_name] relay outputs and inputs without adding more relays or using up extra space. They expect that [product_name] relay contacts support varied wiring setups, and seek explanations about the electrical separation and behavior of the relay contacts inside [product_name].
